public_rationale: Multiyear infrastructure development is documented, but that does not establish a typical multiyear construction duration for operational AI data centers. JLL reports an 18-month average for 50 MW data centers, while Epoch discusses gigawatt-scale plans of two years or less. These are material qualifications, but their populations and milestones differ from full AI-project completion. The evidence does not settle the ordinary generalization.
limitations: A completed campus, an operational building and an installed compute cluster have different timelines.
Planned milestones cannot substitute for achieved commissioning dates.
The statement's tentative wording is preserved rather than converted into a universal rule.

our_interpretation: This is a tentative empirical generalization about typical construction time, not an unconditional assertion that every project takes years.
I read years as a duration of at least two years for a typical new large AI data center.

The surrounding discussion requires distinguishing construction-to-operation of the stated project scope from opening its first building. Later optional campus expansions should not extend the original completion date.
I use August 2026, the latest completed calendar month before publication, for the prevailing construction conditions. Earlier project records are context unless they establish those conditions.
The author's personal source access is not independently testable and is not treated as a forecast condition.
criteria.support_condition: Representative records for comparable new large AI projects establish that typical construction-to-operational-completion durations under prevailing conditions are at least two years.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative comparable records establish typical construction-to-operational-completion durations below two years. An isolated rapid conversion or first-phase opening is insufficient.
